description: Persist pending mention dismissals in the database so they survive Redis cache expiry/restart. Create a pending_mention_dismissals table, model, and integrate with PendingMentionCache populate/extend and the destroy action.
steps: 1. Create migration for pending_mention_dismissals table with account_id (bigint, not null), notification_id (bigint, not null), created_at, and unique index on [account_id, notification_id].
2. Create PendingMentionDismissal model with belongs_to associations and validations.
3. Modify PendingMentionCache.populate and PendingMentionCache.extend to exclude dismissed notification_ids by querying the dismissals table.
4. Modify Api::V1::PendingMentionsController#destroy to persist a row to the dismissals table in addition to redis.zrem.
acceptance_criteria: A new pending_mention_dismissals table exists with the correct schema
When a mention is dismissed, a row is written to the database
When populate or extend rebuilds the cache, dismissed notification_ids are excluded
All Ruby files pass syntax checks
verification: Run ruby -c on all modified/created Ruby files
Run rubocop on modified files if available
findings: All steps completed. Migration creates pending_mention_dismissals table with unique index on [account_id, notification_id]. Model uses create_or_find_by for race-safe upserts. Both populate and extend methods now batch-query dismissals alongside favourites and replies. Pre-commit hooks (rubocop, lint-staged) pass after bundle install resolved missing gems.
